title: Planter's Almanac
subtitle: Your starter kit, grow-light picks, watering how-tos & water guide — all editable in almanac.json.

sections.title: Beginner Playbook
sections.intro: The handful of habits that prevent most plant deaths — especially in a cool, low-light home.

items.name: Water the plant, not the calendar
items.detail: Finger-check 2" down; only water if dry. Overwatering is the #1 killer here.

items.name: Drainage holes, always
items.detail: And empty the saucer after watering.

items.name: Quarantine newcomers ~2 weeks
items.detail: Watch for hitchhiking pests before mixing them in.

items.name: Settle before repotting
items.detail: Let a new plant adjust 1–2 weeks; don't repot day one.

items.name: Rotate + wipe leaves
items.detail: Even growth, and dust-free leaves use what little light you have.

items.name: Read the leaves
items.detail: Yellow = usually overwatering; crispy tips = under-water / dry air; leggy = more light.

items.name: Skip feeding props & winter
items.detail: No fertilizer on unrooted cuttings or during dormancy.

sections.title: Soil & Amendments
sections.intro: Keep these on hand; you'll combine them three ways.

items.name: Potting mix
items.detail: Peat/coir base. Coco coir is the greener peat alternative.

items.name: Perlite
items.detail: The #1 amendment — aeration + drainage.

items.name: Orchid bark
items.detail: Chunky aroid-mix ingredient.

items.name: Pumice
items.detail: Heavier aeration that won't float; ideal for gritty succulent mixes.

items.name: Horticultural charcoal
items.detail: Keeps soil & water-props fresh.

items.name: Worm castings
items.detail: Gentle organic nutrients.

items.name: Aroids — Monstera, Snow Queen, Brasil
items.detail: potting mix + perlite + bark

items.name: Semi-succulents — String of Hearts, Hoya
items.detail: gritty: 50–70% pumice / perlite / coarse sand

items.name: Everyday — Pilea, Tradescantia, Money Tree
items.detail: potting mix + extra perlite

sections.title: Tools
sections.intro: A small kit covers everything you own.

items.name: Sharp, clean snips
items.detail: Propagation + pruning.

items.name: Chopstick / skewer
items.detail: Aerate soil, test moisture, stake cuttings.

items.name: Microfiber cloth
items.detail: Wiping leaves genuinely matters in low light.

items.name: Hygrometer + pebble/humidity tray
items.detail: Track and nudge your 45–55% RH.

items.name: Pest kit
items.detail: Rubbing alcohol + swabs, neem oil or insecticidal soap.

items.name: Rooting hormone (optional) + gloves
items.detail: Gloves for Rubber & Tradescantia sap.

sections.title: Grow Lights
sections.intro: Full-spectrum white, 4000–6500K (skip the 'blurple' ones), 12–14 hrs/day on a timer, ~10–14" above foliage. Aimed at your String of Hearts & Hoya.

items.name: GooingTop clip (~$25) — top pick
items.detail: Dual gooseneck clips to a sill; 6000K full-spectrum, 5-level dimmer, 4/8/12h timer, runs cool. Ideal for 1–3 plants.

items.name: SANSI 36W bulb (E26)
items.detail: Drop into a lamp you already own; ceramic heat-dissipation keeps it cool.

items.name: Barrina T5 strips (~$25–40)
items.detail: For a future shelf; full-spectrum ~5000K, linkable, but mount 3–12" close.

items.name: Soltech Aspect (~$150)
items.detail: Design-forward pendant that fits a Japandi space; no built-in timer.

sections.note: Your String of Hearts wants 4–6 hrs of bright indirect light daily — more than the bay window reliably gives, which is why a light earns its keep.

sections.title: Bottom Watering
sections.intro: Works for all your soil-potted plants — deeper roots, dry foliage, less rot.

items.name: Soak
items.detail: Sit the pot in 1–2" of water for 10–20 min until the topsoil feels damp.

items.name: Drain fully
items.detail: Lift and let it drip out — never leave it sitting.

items.name: Semi-succulents
items.detail: Keep the String of Hearts / Hoya soak brief.

sections.note: Bottom watering doesn't flush salts — top-water every ~4th–6th time to rinse mineral buildup. N/A for cuttings still rooting in water (Brasil, Hoya, Rubber).

sections.title: Water Quality
sections.intro: Your plants are the tap-tolerant kind, so you likely don't need distilled. Upgrade only if you see crispy tips or white crust on terracotta.

items.name: Carbon filter (Brita/faucet) — cheapest
items.detail: Removes chlorine; note that letting tap sit out only offgasses chlorine, not chloramine or minerals.

items.name: Countertop distiller (~$60–90)
items.detail: Very pure, but slow (a gallon at a time) and uses electricity.

items.name: Countertop / under-sink RO
items.detail: Scales better; can remineralize; wastes ~1/3 to drain.

items.name: Remineralize distilled/RO
items.detail: It's mineral-free — add a Cal-Mag or a balanced feed.

items.name: Never use softened water
items.detail: Its sodium builds up in soil and blocks water uptake.

sections.note: Greenest + cheapest for ~10 tap-tolerant plants: a carbon filter or collected rainwater, saving fancier water for any plant that shows mineral stress. Want zero variables? A countertop distiller + Cal-Mag is the least-hassle.
